answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks through memory-bandwidth challenges governed by an execution kernel. To validate an identity, an agent must run memory-hard access traversals that mirror a deterministic cryptographic graph. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of provisioning dedicated physical DRAM channels rather than multiplexing virtual nodes. However, an opal haze of memory bus saturation can throttle co-located workloads and penalize low-power agents.
